result.title: S1-Evo: Experience-Guided Evidence Competition Attacks on Typed System-1 Decision Models
result.summary: Typed System-1 (S1) decision models are increasingly deployed in LLM agents for routing, moderation, and authorization to cut inference cost, yet untrusted context can still manipulate typed outputs and alter execution branches. Unlike autoregressive System-2 (S2) models, S1 interfaces score dynamic rules and options without token-by-token decoding, mismatching attacks targeting text continuation or explicit override commands. We propose S1-Evo, a self-evolving framework tailored to S1's contract-based option competition and margin feedback. S1-Evo perturbs untrusted fields via contract-aware evidence channels to induce \emph{evidence competition} with original task evidence while preserving fact invariance. Offline on seed tasks, it optimizes candidates via feedback search guided by directional margins and re-verification, distilling verified flips into experience cards. At test time, S1-Evo retrieves relevant cards to construct perturbations for unseen tasks. Across four benchmarks and three S1 models, S1-Evo reaches 71.99\% mean ASR and 57.47\% high-confidence ASR on \texttt{jev-1.14}, and causes up to 24.00\% E2E agent violations.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 S1-Evo，针对 LLM agent 中 typed System-1 决策模型（路由、审核、授权）的对抗攻击框架：通过 contract-aware 证据通道扰动不可信字段，使注入证据与原任务证据竞争，并用方向性 margin 反馈搜索离线优化候选、蒸馏为经验卡片，测试时检索迁移到未见任务。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「证据竞争」与按通道注入混淆证据的探测方式，可能为检验 VLM 决策究竟依赖视觉证据还是文本旁路、以及证据冲突下的归因与筛选提供可核查的评测思路；但论文对象是文本 typed 输出与 agent 执行分支，与 latent 视觉推理状态无直接联系，借鉴价值需进一步核查。
